t: This is a statue of Sir Robert Clayton, standing at the entrance to the North Wing of St Thomas' Hospital in Lambeth. It was carved around the turn of the eighteenth century by Grinling Gibbons, the Anglo-Dutch sculptor and wood carver whose work also appears at Hampton Court and St Paul's. Clayton was a banker, a politician and Lord Mayor of London. As President of the hospital, he oversaw its complete rebuilding, along with its church, in the late seventeenth century, which is why he is honoured here. The statue is Grade I listed.
